name: Influence without Authority
definition: Leaders lead by communicating their ideas clearly. We drive alignment through data and insights. We create an environment where knowledge trumps position.

rows.situation: When the people you need do not report to you
rows.under: Escalates so the work gets assigned to them.
rows.justRight: Makes the case in their terms, with what it is worth to their goals, and lets them choose.
rows.over: Spends months building consensus on something you could simply have decided.

rows.under: Wins on volume, seniority, or persistence.
rows.justRight: Brings the number, the customer evidence, or the experiment that settles it.
rows.over: Demands data for decisions too small or too fast to be worth measuring.

rows.situation: When you could just pull rank
rows.under: Pulls rank as the first move. People comply and do not believe it.
rows.justRight: Explains until people are convinced, and keeps rank for the rare case where speed beats agreement.
rows.over: Refuses to ever decide, so the team waits for a consensus that never forms.

rows.situation: When the best idea comes from the most junior person
rows.under: Lets it go unheard because of where it came from.
rows.justRight: Takes it, credits it, and makes the source visible so it happens again.
rows.over: Overcorrects until seniority and experience become disqualifying.

rows.situation: When the argument has to travel without you
rows.under: Relies on the meeting. The idea dies when you leave the room.
rows.justRight: Writes it down clearly enough that someone who was not there can act on it.
rows.over: Writes a document for every decision, until reading becomes the bottleneck.

rows.situation: When you did not persuade them
rows.under: Escalates the same argument to their manager, unchanged.
rows.justRight: Finds out what would change their mind, and either comes back with that or drops it.
rows.over: Keeps relitigating with new framing until the relationship costs more than the decision.
